addedLines: Artifact: publishes pages on claude.ai; reads claude.ai artifact links. Load it with ToolSearch (select:Artifact) before writing any document, plan, analysis or visual, and whenever other people come up as readers, even after the work is written. Its description says whether to publish, offer a page or do neither. What follows applies whether or not it is loaded yet. Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL. When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A write-up that will be posted in a channel or a thread is still published, so the post can carry the link; when it is short, Claude also gives the text in its reply, ready to paste. When it might be passed along but nothing says so, Claude offers the page in one line instead of saying nothing. When the person asks for the file itself, such as "just give me the .html file" or "save these notes as a .md file", Claude gives them that file and does not publish it.

Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. <?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

attachment.content:
- animation-vocabulary: Reverse-lookup glossary that turns a vague description of a web animation or motion effect into its exact term ("the bouncy thing when a popover opens" → Pop in; "the iOS rubber-band scroll" → Rubber-banding). Use when the user asks "what's it called when…", or describes a motion effect without knowing its name and wants the right word to prompt an AI or designer with. For naming an effect, not designing or building one.
- apple-design: Apple's approach to interface design and fluid, physical motion, translated for the web. Use when building or reviewing gesture-driven UI, spring animations, drag/swipe/sheet interactions, momentum and interruptible transitions, translucent materials and depth, typography (optical sizing, tracking, leading), reduced-motion, or the design foundations (feedback, spatial consistency, restraint) behind Apple-style interfaces.
- emil-design-eng: This skill encodes Emil Kowalski's philosophy on UI polish, component design, animation decisions, and the invisible details that make software feel great.
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- self-code-review: Deep, evidence-based self review of the current branch against its base. Use when the user asks to "self review", "review my branch", "review my PR", "review my code", "review my changes", or wants a thorough pre-push critique.

  fewer. Explain only when asked.
- Surface non-trivial design decisions before baking them into a plan or an
  implementation.

Steffen Grabert, steffen.grabert@tum.de

TUM student. Python for data, ML and finance; TypeScript for web and
desktop. Recurring domains: investing and portfolio modelling, football
analytics, study tools.

# AGENTS.md

Rules for AI coding agents in this repo. Humans follow them too.

Hackathon repo, EHL Grand Finale, Munich, 10 to 11 Oct 2026. Code freeze and Live Final Sunday
12:00. Working agent first, polish second.

## Rules

- Do not preserve backward compatibility. Remove obsolete paths instead of adding layers,
  fallbacks or migrations.
- Choose the simplest implementation that fully meets the current requirement. No speculative
  abstractions, configuration or indirection.
- Grow in layers on a product that already works. Never trade a working agent for unfinished
  complexity.
- Keep components modular and concerns separated.
- Read `arena_kit` (in `.venv`) before writing a helper: cost function, quote parsing, data lookup
  and runners exist. We wrap the kit, never patch it. Guide:
  https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit/tree/main/starter-kit
- Never commit secrets. Keys live in `.env`. Never print, log or paste the arena key anywhere.
- All changes go through a PR against `main`, reviewed by one teammate. Branch `<firstname>/<topic>`.
  Agents may commit, push their branch and `gh pr create`; never push to `main`, force-push or merge.
- Run `uv run pytest -q && uv run ruff check .` before every PR.
- No em-dashes in prose or copy. Be terse: after an action, state what changed in three lines.

## The challenge

We are the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke. Our agent negotiates by e-mail with Tacto's
supplier bots (LLM personas with hidden economics) and closes one term sheet per case, or walks.

- **Score** per case: `(C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)`, clipped to 0..1. C is total cost
  over the horizon (price, uncovered need, payment, freight, lead time, quality, tooling, index
  clause, relationship charge), computed exactly by `arena_kit.total_cost`. No deal scores the
  alternative (0 if none). A broken must-have scores 0.
- **Live Final**: five waves of hidden cases, 8 minutes each, a wave's cases in parallel. Wave
  score = mean case score x 100; total = sum. New suppliers; up to a third mix supplier and case
  types practice never shows; some cite the Sunday 08:00 data release.

**Hard rules, breaking one can disqualify us:**
- No human in the loop during the final. The runner starts before 12:00 and is left alone.
- Agent code never calls `/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`,
  `/leaderboard`, `/v1/leaderboard`, `/results`, `/v1/results`.
- One key per team. No attacks on the arena or other teams (prompt-injecting bots counts).
- The final runs the commit we submit at 12:00. No pushes after that.

**Hard limits:**
- 60 s per message per thread from the supplier's reply; three timeouts in a row end the thread.
- 10 messages per thread, up to 3 term sheets per message, every sheet carries every `negotiable`
  field.
- Max 3 claim checks per message, one per sentence, ID and figure in the same sentence. A wrong
  figure or unknown ID is `contradicted` and costs trust.
- 10 calls/s and 10 open sessions per key.
- **Practice quota: 200 sessions per rolling 24 h for the whole team.** Sandbox (`case:D01`,
  `case:D02`) and the local simulator are free.

## Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `docs/learnings.md` | **read first**: what we know about the arena, suppliers and data, with evidence |
| `docs/design.md` | the agent we are building: modules, data, policy, build order |
| `docs/challenge.md`, `api.md`, `submission.md` | Tacto's brief, API and cost formula, hand-in (upstream copies) |
| `buyer/policy.py`, `runner.py` | the price engine: per-thread policy and the loop that plays a case (`docs/design.md`, Implemented) |
| `buyer/economics.py`, `claims.py`, `personas.py`, `writer.py`, `llm.py` | C and term planning, claim bank, persona signals, e-mail and model paragraph |
| `buyer/cli.py` | `buyer play`, `buyer run`, `buyer pull` |
| `tests/` | end to end against `arena-sim`, no network, no model |
| `exports/` | Saturday probe sessions as CSV/JSONL; schema in `exports/README.md` |
| `analysis/explore.py` | data package exploration: profiles, persona signals, report page |
| `data/package/` | the data package (gitignored); Sunday also `data/release-sunday/` |
| `logs/sessions/<set>/` | finished sessions with trace and back office (gitignored; Saturday's committed with `-f`) |
| `logs/runs/`, `logs/practice-v*.log` | our decisions per move (anchor, terms, claims, prices) and the practice run logs |

The MCP server `arena-data` (`.mcp.json`) gives SQL, ID lookup and documents over the package.

## Commands

```sh
uv sync                                         # install (Python 3.12)
uv run arena data                               # data package into data/
uv run arena me                                 # key works? quota left?
uv run buyer play case:D01 -v                   # sandbox: free
uv run buyer play case:P01 -v                   # practice: costs 1 of the team's 200
uv run buyer run --set practice --parallel 10   # all hosted practice cases: costs 10
uv run buyer pull --set practice                # finished sessions -> logs/sessions/
uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package   # local API, scripted supplier
uv run --with pandas python analysis/explore.py # data package -> analysis/out/
```

`--agent naive` plays the kit's baseline instead of ours.

## Working on the negotiation agent

- **Code owns numbers, the model owns words.** Every binding value (sheet, accept, walk away) is
  computed or checked in code with `total_cost` and `must_haves_ok`; every figure in an e-mail
  comes from code next to its data ID.
- **Never accept** a sheet that breaks a must-have or costs more than the alternative. Price
  unstated fields at the supplier's standard terms (`arena_kit.docs.standard_terms`).
- **Read the supplier.** What moves it is in the data (call notes, letters, news, quote remarks,
  payment history, scorecards). Trade what is cheap for us for what it values.
- **Score every lever per case.** The same term helps in one case and hurts in the next
  (coverage, payment days, start date, index clause, contract length).
- **Generalise.** No logic keyed on case or supplier IDs; runtime knowledge from the data package
  is fine if it works for unseen suppliers.
- **Don't leak** urgency, budget, a missing alternative or the target price.
- **Every model call has a hard timeout** well under 60 s, and the move still goes out if it
  fails. Measure latency per move.

## The learning loop

1. Try on the simulator or sandbox first. Spend practice quota only on a change you expect to
   help; check `uv run arena me` before batch runs.
2. After practice: `uv run buyer pull`, read `logs/sessions/` (trace, back office, cost breakdown).
3. Find why C_deal missed C_best, change the agent, score candidate sheets offline, play again.
4. Record each finding in `docs/learnings.md` in the same PR: date, tag (`arena` / `data` /
   `rules`), finding, evidence (session, case or data ID), consequence for the agent. Untested
   ideas go under Hypotheses; correct or delete entries that turn out wrong. Design changes go
   into `docs/design.md`. No new doc files without a reason.

## Sunday

- 08:00: `uv run arena data` again; the release lands in `data/release-sunday/`.
- 09:00: pre-flight, one practice case through the final machine and setup.
- 11:30: checklist in `docs/submission.md` (key, data, LLM credits, power, no sleep, log file).
- Before 12:00, from `main`: `uv run buyer run --set final --parallel 10 -v 2>&1 | tee logs/final.log`,
  then submit that commit hash on ehl.gg.

- [Research scope: own commits only](research-scope-own-commits.md): consolidating "my research" means Steffen's commits and sessions, not teammates' branches
- [Shared working tree](shared-working-tree.md) — peer sessions commit in the same checkout; re-check git state, never leave temporary constant edits
- [Elicit worktree](elicit-worktree.md) — experiments live in ../ehlcodacabana-elicit on branch steffen/elicit (PR #14), not in the shared checkout

# Writing for the user
The user may not see your tool calls, tool results, or the text you write between them. Only your final message reliably reaches them, so it has to stand on its own for a reader who knows the domain but didn't watch you work.

Rules for that message:
- Lead with the answer or outcome. If something could not be verified, say so first. Keep it short by leaving things out, not by packing them in.
- One idea per sentence, about 20 words, with a verb. Short does not mean clipped: a sentence beats a label with a colon. Start a new sentence instead of joining clauses with a semicolon.
- No em-dashes, no parentheticals, no arrows.
- State facts and conclusions. Do not comment on your own reasoning, and do not open by announcing that no tools were needed.
- Do not refer to anything by a name you made up during the session. Expand uncommon acronyms the first time you use them. Say who wrote a message and what it said, not by number or label.
- Keep code out of prose. Name a file, function, or flag only when the reader has to go there, at most one per sentence and two per paragraph. Describe the rest in words. Commands, snippets, and error text go in a fenced code block.
- Keep numbers out of prose. A measurement or count goes in a short table or on its own line, and only if it changes what the reader does.
- Use a bulleted or numbered list for parallel items: findings, steps, options, files to look at. One or two sentences per bullet, never a paragraph. Bold the first few words of a bullet or paragraph, never a whole sentence. A single point or a line of argument stays in prose.
- No headers in a message under about 500 words. Above that, at most three. If the user asks for no formatting, use none.
- Stop when the content stops. No closing offer, no restating what you did.

You are operating autonomously. The user is not watching in real time and cannot answer questions mid-task, so asking 'Want me to…?' or 'Shall I…?' will block the work. For reversible actions that follow from the original request, proceed without asking. Stop only for destructive actions or genuine scope changes the user must decide. Offering follow-ups after the task is done is fine; asking permission before doing the work is not.

Exception: when the user is describing a problem, asking a question, or thinking out loud rather than requesting a change, the deliverable is your assessment. Report your findings and stop. Don't apply a fix until they ask for one.

Before ending your turn, check your last paragraph. If it is a plan, an analysis, a question, a list of next steps, or a promise about work you have not done ('I'll…', 'let me know when…'), do that work now with tool calls. That includes retrying after errors and gathering missing information yourself. Do not stop because the context or session is long. End your turn only when the task is complete or you are blocked on input only the user can provide.

Before running a command that changes system state (such as restarts, deletes, or config edits), check that the evidence actually supports that specific action. A signal that pattern-matches to a known failure may have a different cause.

# Claude in Chrome browser automation

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## Loading deferred tools

If the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

Reach for this when the task matches an available agent type, when you have independent work to run in parallel, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate it and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps. For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. Once you've delegated a search, don't also run it yourself — wait for the result.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

Preview feature:
Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations
- Diagram variations
- Configuration examples

Preview content is rendered as markdown in a monospace box. Multi-line text with newlines is supported. When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. Do not use previews for simple preference questions where labels and descriptions suffice. Note: previews are only supported for single-select questions (not multiSelect).

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

content.content:
# Agent design

The target architecture of our buyer, merged from the team's planning notes (PRs #7 to #10,
10 Oct). What we learned in play is in `learnings.md`; this file says what we build.

**Status.** The branch `steffen/price-engine` plays a code-only policy with a model-written
paragraph (`buyer/policy.py`, run by `buyer/runner.py`): practice mean of best scores 0.73 (from
0.32), sandbox D01 0.99, D02 0.73. What it does is under "Implemented" below; the rest of this file
is the target design. Julian's draft two (`origin/julian/draft-two`) holds a richer stance and
reader design that is not merged. The architecture diagram is on page 1 of
[how-it-works.pdf](how-it-works.pdf).

## Implemented (price engine)

| Module | Job |
|---|---|
| `buyer/economics.py` | C of a sheet; the accept gate (`deal_cost`); what a sheet is worth to the supplier (`supplier_value` plus overtime for a faster delivery than it quoted); term planning: every allowed combination priced at the supplier's own valuation, lowest C, ties to the supplier's side; the relationship-optimal price |
| `buyer/claims.py` | claim bank: should-cost below its price, our order prices, each cost driver's largest fall over any window up to 12 months, notice period, forecast, scorecard, case rival quotes, hedge and open-book notes; rival offers in an RFQ |
| `buyer/personas.py` | owner type, persona signals from notes, letters, quote remarks and news, cost of money |
| `buyer/policy.py` | per thread: anchor by goal and persona, 30 % of the gap per round, held low after a deep first concession, patience budget for near-cost, fully booked and relationship-goal suppliers; adopts its counter terms when they cost us less, mirrors a better alternative, takes a required index clause; claims 3 in round 1, then 1 per round; close on final offer, agreement or round limit |
| `buyer/reader.py` | the supplier's asks from its fixed sentences (volume, proof, faster payment, our target); no model |
| `buyer/writer.py`, `buyer/llm.py` | the e-mail: a model paragraph that answers the supplier's last e-mail and its asks (no digits, IDs or leaks, else the template), then code sentences with figures (the binding volume), claims and the proposal from code; the forecast rows as a CSV when proof is asked |
| `buyer/runner.py` | one message at a time per session, to the thread whose 60 s clock has run longest; keepalive questions for finished bidders; rollback when a send times out; a guarded move resends our last sheet; the model's time budgeted so every live clock still gets a message; a terminal reply ends the case; accept the cheapest standing sheet that keeps the must-haves and beats the alternative (relationship charge included), after a refused close decide again on what stands; Live Final waves that never raise and resume a crashed case |

## Principle

Code owns every number and every binding decision; the model reads replies and writes e-mails.
Score is total cost C, not price. Every step has a fallback that still sends a move within 60 s.

## A case

1. **Prepare** (before the first move, about 20 s): open the session, build a case brief: C_open,
   C_alt, target, walk-away, the lever table (C of each allowed option), a view of each supplier,
   and a claim bank of verified arguments. A stance call proposes per-supplier parameters; code
   clamps them.
2. **Negotiate**, one thread negotiator per supplier, in parallel. Each round:

   ```
   supplier reply
     -> READ    (model, hard timeout)  offer, intent, objections, statements
     -> CHECK   (code)  supplier statements against the data
     -> PLAN    (code)  candidate sheets scored with total_cost, filtered by must_haves_ok
     -> DECIDE  (code)  counter / accept / walk away, move size, claims
     -> WRITE   (model, hard timeout; template if late)  figures and IDs injected by code
     -> GUARD   (code)  every negotiable field, claim format, no leaks, no unplanned figures
   ```

3. **Close**: accept the best sheet that keeps every must-have and beats C_alt, or walk away;
   at the latest 90 s before the wave's 8-minute cap.
4. **Learn**: store the trace and what we learned per supplier for the next practice run.

## Modules

  quote minus an assumed margin. A relationship charge in a practice result reveals the true margin.
- **Cost of money**: cash discounts, cash-need notes, credit index, equity ratio. Seen rates: 0 to
  17 %/yr (`learnings.md`).

| Constant | Values |
|---|---|

suppliers, up to a third of cases mixing supplier and case types practice never showed, some
citing the 08:00 release. Research on Saturday 10 October, evening: the kit's code, all 21 case
files, `logs/runs/`, `exports/`, the data package, and our agent on `arena-sim`. No practice
quota spent. Same conventions as `learnings.md`: date, tag, finding, evidence, consequence.

## Verdict

The code runs on every case structure we know. Its tuning is in-sample and unmeasured beyond
the ten hosted cases. The biggest gaps for Sunday: new suppliers get a neutral profile because
the release's letters and news never reach the persona code; one exception loses a whole case
(or every later wave); four or more bidders time out.

| # | Risk | Damage | Fix | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | an exception in a move or the wave poll | a case at its alternative (0 in 6 of 21), or all later waves | catch per move, keep polling | small |
| 2 | release rows invisible to SQL; most suppliers without text | neutral profile for new suppliers | read release rows via the ID index; scan the supplier's e-mails | small to medium |
| 3 | 4 or more bidders | timeouts, lost patience, ended threads | stop sending to the worst bidders after round 1 | medium, a tactics decision |
| 4 | missed phrasings in `SIGNALS` | traits not detected | widen to word stems | small |
| 5 | `price_unit` ignored | wrong-direction rival or order-price claims | divide by `price_unit` | small |

  including the nine never hosted (P06, P09, P12 to P17, P19), played through `arena-sim`
  in-process with our agent and the package, no model: no exception, 0 to 1 s per case. Covers

  combinations (P09). The sim's supplier is a fixed script, so this checks code paths, not
  tactics. → Worth a test in `tests/` that plays every case file from `GET /v1/cases` this way
  (load them into `Sim(cases, pkg.facts)`, strip the `hosted` key).
- 2026-10-10 `rules` **One exception loses a case.** `play_case` has no guard around
  `Negotiator.setup` or `move`. Fields a hidden case may lack crash it: a rival quote without
  `unit_price` (`claims.py` `rival_quote`), an index clause without `material_share`
  (`writer.py` `FIELDS`), a scorecard without `quarter` (`claims.py` `scorecard`), a month not in
  `YYYY-MM` (`months_back`). The session then sits until the wave cap, which scores the
  alternative (0 in D01, P05, P06, P10, P14, P17). → Catch per move; on error send our last
  sheet again with the template e-mail.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` **One error stops the final.** `runner.play_waves` re-raises any non-403
  `ArenaError` from the case-list poll, and a network error after the client's retries is not
  caught at all (`arena_kit/client.py` `_call`). Every later wave is then lost; no human may
  restart. → Catch everything in the poll loop, log, sleep, poll again; a crashed case resumes
  with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` (a second `POST` is a 409 naming the session).

- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Four bidders or more time out.** The arena answers one call per session at
  a time (`arena_kit/client.py`: "a call may wait for another call on the same session first").
  Supplier replies took 19 s median, 28 s p90 (121 moves in `logs/runs/`); our writer 1.8 s
  median, 6.3 s max (73 calls, none failed, 7 dropped by the filter). A thread waits about
  (N - 1) x 21 s for its next message against a 60 s limit:

  | Bidders | Wait at median | Wait at p90 | Rounds per thread in 390 s |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 2 | 23 s | 34 s | 9 / 6 |
  | 3 | 44 s | 66 s, late | 6 / 4 |
  | 4 | 65 s, late | late | 5 / 3 |

  P05 (3 bidders) had one late move in v5. No case file has more than 3 bidders, but hidden
  cases bring "new settings". → With 4 or more bidders, stop sending to the clearly worst ones
  after round 1; the writer's 20 s timeout matters little next to the supplier's reply time.

### Data and the Sunday release

- 2026-10-10 `rules` **The release reaches only part of the agent.** `DataPackage` finds
  `data/release-sunday/` next to the package, merges its `facts.json` (new IDs only) and puts its
  `data/*.csv` rows into the ID index for `lookup` and `ids`, never into SQLite
  (`arena_kit/data.py`, `_ids`). `personas.profile()`, `Negotiator.full_cost()` and the claims
  built from SQL (`po_lines`, `cost_drivers`, `documents`, `suppliers`) never see release rows,
  and document files resolve against the package root, not the release. Release IDs can still be
  cited. `design.md` says the release is "read at runtime"; that holds for `facts.json` only.
  → Read release rows through `pkg.ids(prefix)` / `pkg.lookup` (each row carries `root`) in
  `profile()` and the document claims. Check the CSV schema at 08:00.
- 2026-10-10 `data` **Most suppliers have no text.** Of 447 suppliers, 46 have documents, 31 news,
  18 quote remarks; the other 401 get the neutral profile (rate 7 %, no signals). A new supplier
  in the final is one of them or unknown to the package. → Its own e-mails and the release are
  the only persona source.
- 2026-10-10 `data` 15 of 108 quotes are priced per 100 (13) or per 1000 (2) pieces
  (`quotes.price_unit`). Rival-quote and order-history claims compare `unit_price` with the
  supplier's per-piece price without converting. → Divide by `price_unit` before comparing.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Structures only in unplayed cases** (case files): `tooling_eur` negotiable
  and lead time at most 84 days (P06), chargeback in the alternative (P12), index series PPI-C241
  in a clause (P16), fixed payment in a quality case (P12), a 3-part bundle (P15). Every case type
  and category goal appears in at least one hosted case. Only `incoterm` (D02) lies outside the
  fields the planner knows.

- 2026-10-10 `data` **The patterns are not fitted to the practice suppliers**: the package's text
  is generated and its phrases recur, so all 10 suppliers of the unplayed cases get at least one
  trait. They miss other forms of the same phrases: "restructuring programme with its banks"
  (sup:70150), "negotiating with its banks" (sup:70280), "lowered its rating" (sup:70310),
  "bought their nickel and alloys forward" (sup:70730), "advertising free machine capacity"
  (sup:70250), "allocated in line with last year's call-offs" (sup:70410). "I cannot sign
  anything that lowers our margin now" (5 call notes) is a trait with no pattern. → Widen to word

  70250, DEMO-J1; capacity_full sup:70240; cash_need sup:70210), including a sandbox supplier the
  package does not know. → Scanning each reply gives unknown suppliers a profile (untested in
  play).

- 2026-10-10 `arena` **Out-of-sample performance is unmeasured.** The 0.727 mean is in-sample:
  every constant was tuned on the same ten hosted cases and the other nine cannot be played.
  Runs of one case spread widely across v1 to v6 (P18 0.25 to 0.49 over seven runs, P08 0.40 to
  0.55), and with a model-written paragraph the wording changes per run while wording moves the
  price (`learnings.md`, takeaway 3). → Treat single-run moves below about 0.1 as noise.

  | Constant | Cases behind it | Risk |
  |---|---|---|
  | `ANCHOR` leverage 0.78 | P05, P08 / P18 (one template) | medium |
  | `ANCHOR` routine 0.82 | P07 (P04 overridden by price_frozen) | medium to high |
  | `ANCHOR` quality_first 0.88 | P11 | medium |
  | `ANCHOR` stabilise 0.92, secure_supply 0.88 | none: always overridden in practice | high, untested |
  | `FRACTION` 0.3 | D01, D02, all hosted cases | low |
  | `DEEP` 0.06 | P05 (two job shops), D02 | medium |
  | price_frozen 0.95 | P03, P04 | low to medium |
  | capacity_full 0.93, budget 0.16, overtime 0.005 | P10, P05 sup:70240 | medium |
  | `near_cost` 0.97, budget 0.14 | P02 | high |

1. `uv run arena data`; confirm `DataPackage("data/package").release` is not `None`.
2. List the release's `data/*.csv` and their columns; count supplier IDs new vs in the package.
3. Run every case file through `arena-sim` again with the release loaded.

  | `DEEP` 0.06 | P05 (two job shops), D02 | medium |

  | capacity_full 0.93, budget 0.16, overtime 0.005 | P10, P05 sup:70240 | medium |
  | `near_cost` 0.97, budget 0.14 | P02 | high |

  → A hidden `stabilise` or `secure_supply` case with no override opens at an anchor never played.

1. `uv run arena data`; confirm `DataPackage("data/package").release` is not `None`.
2. List the release's `data/*.csv` and their columns; count supplier IDs new vs in the package.
3. Run every case file through `arena-sim` again with the release loaded.

# Learnings

What we know about the arena, its supplier bots and the data package, and what it means for the
agent. Basis, Saturday 10 October: 15 practice sessions covering all 10 hosted cases and 12
suppliers, 17 sandbox sessions, the team's simulator and sandbox experiments, and the data
package. Every euro figure and what-if score below was recomputed with `arena_kit.total_cost`. Evidence: `exports/` (every session, supplier thread,
e-mail and claim; schema in `exports/README.md`) and `analysis/explore.py` (the data package).

Add findings to the matching section, newest first: date, tag, the finding, its evidence (case,
session or data ID) and what it means for the agent. Tags: `arena` seen in a session, `data` from
the data package, `rules` from `docs/api.md` or the kit's code. Untested ideas go under
Hypotheses. Correct or delete entries that turn out wrong.

## Takeaways for the agent

1. **Stay below the supplier's counter until the end; it agrees the moment our sheet reaches the
   counter it would make.** D01: our 51.25 one cent under its 51.30 was agreed at once
   (sandbox `14ea35524959126f`). Moving a share of the gap each round keeps it conceding: the
   engine took the practice mean of best scores from 0.32 to 0.73.
2. **Verified claims that it "took into account" lower where it stops, most of all in round 1.**
   D01 with the same price path: no claims 50.00, delivery record 49.60, notice 49.60, should-cost
   49.30, three claims spread over rounds 48.90 (score 0.998). Which types count differs by
   supplier (table under Arguments and claims).
3. **Words move it too.** D01, identical sheets, no claims: plain 50.00, "firm" 49.90, warm and
   acknowledging its wage costs 49.60, "What would you need from us to move further on the
   price?" 49.40 (0.987). But a question repeated every round backfires: practice suppliers
   answered "volume!" where volume is fixed and stopped moving (P05, P18 v3). Answer what it
   asked; state a fixed volume as our full demand, with the figure.
4. **Patience is a budget of about 40 % cumulative gap** (sum over rounds of our sheet's distance
   to its counter, relative to its price): final offers at 41 to 42 % (D01 linear paths), 39 %
   (P07), 42 % (P08), 36 % (P18). Suppliers selling near our should-cost or with a pricing
   committee end much earlier: Nordmark walked away at 19 % (P02 v1), Ravensteiner gave its final
   offer in round 1 at a 15 % gap (P10 v1).
5. **Choose terms by C at the supplier's own valuation**, including a contract beyond our horizon
   (free for us, security for it) and the overtime a fully booked supplier charges for faster
   delivery (about 0.5 % of the price per day: Hrvelec, Ravensteiner). This alone moved P10 from
   a 42-day to a 56-day lead time.
6. **In relationship goals stop at the price where C is lowest.** D01: all claims at once pushed
   to 48.50 and scored 0.969; stopping near 48.90 scored 0.998, the relationship charge grows
   faster below.
7. **Only a supplier's standing sheet can be accepted** (an alternative returns 422). A better
   alternative is sent back as our sheet; it agrees and becomes standing (P10).
8. **Raw-material distributors refuse a fixed price beyond 12 months and refuse any deadband**
   (P08, P18): take their clause and negotiate the price; insisting on a deadband stalled them.
   But only when their sheet with the clause costs us less than their last one: Nordmark's copper
   clause came alone and cost 1.8 % of spend, score 0 (P02 `680eb11405186b42`,
   `d52ccdd3d2e07b3f`). That rule separates all 24 P02, P08 and P18 sessions correctly.
9. **RFQ: the arena answers one call per session at a time** and each thread's 60 s clock runs
   from its reply, so sends are serialized by deadline; the cheapest rival offer is a new,
   verified claim to every other bidder every round (P05 0.83, D02 0.73).
10. **The ceiling is lower than 0.9.** Best per case over all teams averages 0.82 (`/v1/live`,
    Saturday evening); practice C_best for P04 needs 4.93 against a frozen 4.94.

## Where we stand

Best score per hosted case, Saturday 22:00: mean 0.776 (team rank 4 of 24 on the practice board;
first place 0.838). Record = best of all teams on `/v1/live` at about 20:30 (house agent in brackets).

| Case | Goal | Ours | Session | Deal | Record (house) | What limits us |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P01 | stabilise | 0.974 | `4cc256188e1cd8af` | 130.18, Nov, 14 d | 0.995 (0.966) | agreed at our sheet in round 4 |
| P02 | stabilise | 0.735 | `practice-v11-P02.log` | 361.67, 90 d, CU clause 5 % deadband | 0.847 (0.740) | agreed at once at our relationship optimum; the charge (not the price) caps the score |
| P03 | stabilise | 0.923 | `c7fcc4c7ae8f4e9a` | 432.15, 90 d, 24 m | 0.936 (0.925) | price frozen |
| P04 | routine | 0.860 | `81e9fd209c3fd659` | 4.94, 90 d, 36 m | 0.874 (0.860) | C_best needs 4.93 |
| P05 | leverage RFQ | 0.828 | `917135b8156fb8a3` | Dralveck 27.86, 14 d, 35 d | 0.824 (0.555) | ours is the record |
| P07 | routine | 0.751 | `cacd5028b34d30dc` | 5.35, 45 d, 36 m | 0.779 (0.782) | final offer in round 3 |
| P08 | leverage | 0.670 | `practice-v10.log` | 5.26, AS-14404 clause | 0.916 (0.752) | first counter 5.40 with the falling-driver claims; final offer in round 3 to 4 |
| P10 | secure_supply | 0.679 | `7c4f1855794797d6` | 31.50, 56 d, 36 m | 0.702 (0.686) | fully booked, final early |
| P11 | quality_first | 0.710 | `3ac9ee6cf673cf7c` | 45.50, 300 ppm | 0.807 (0.314) | wants faster payment, which is fixed |
| P18 | leverage | 0.621 | `practice-v10.log` | 5.10, AS-14404 clause | 0.677 (0.386) | first counter 5.30 with the falling-driver claims, path 5.20, 5.10 repeats exactly |

## Score and terms

- 2026-10-10 `rules` **The category goal sets the rates of C**, not the case type (P13 is a price
  increase under `leverage`, P06 an RFQ under `stabilise`). From all 21 case files:

  | Goal | Fallback risk | Relationship charge | Push for |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `leverage` | 3 % (D02: 5 %) | no | price: rival quotes, should-cost, indices |
  | `routine` | 5 % | no | price and a quick close; small stakes |
  | `quality_first` | 8 % | no | low `ppm_commitment`, chargeback at least `cost_per_defect` |
  | `stabilise` | 10 % | yes, sustainable margin 0.5 to 8 % | structure: term, start date, payment, fair clause |
  | `secure_supply` | 25 % | yes, 4 to 10 % | full coverage and lead time first, then price |

- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Every session reveals C_best, also a walk-away**, plus our cost breakdown
  computed with the supplier's true numbers, relationship charge included. D01 walk-away after
  one message: c_open 448,810.67, c_best 408,623.99. → One session per case gives its target,
  and a relationship charge gives the supplier's true margin, i.e. its full cost.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Uncovered need** costs `fallback_unit_price` plus `fallback_risk_pct` % of
  it; coverage is `min(volume, need) x min(months / 12, horizon)`. Committed volume above the need
  is bought anyway; months beyond the horizon neither cost nor earn. Evidence and examples:
  takeaway 2.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Index clause** cost: `spend x material_share x (|path| - deadband)`, signed
  like the case's `index_paths`, plus `index_risk_pct` % of `spend x material_share` whenever a
  clause exists. Only a falling path larger than the risk charge makes a clause pay.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Late delivery** is `late_cost_per_day x days beyond need_lead_time_days`,
  one sum per case. Must-haves can cap the lead time (P05: at most 42 days).
- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Effective date:** units bought before it cost the current price, so a
  later start is worth months x volume x price step. Negotiable in D01, P01, P13. D01 at 50.90
  and 24 months: April instead of December start, 0.73 to 0.81; plus 60-day payment, 0.87.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Our money:** 8 % a year and reference 60 days in all 21 cases. Paying 30
  days earlier costs 0.67 % of spend.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Relationship charge** (`stabilise`, `secure_supply`) grows with the square
  of the first 5 missing margin points, so the cheapest deal sits below the sustainable margin
  (D01: about 2 points below its 4 %) unless the supplier's cost floor binds first. It also
  moves with payment terms: P02 carried 5,483 at 368.70 and 90 days, 901 at 366.41 and 14 days.
- 2026-10-10 `arena` D01's deal at 50.90 carried no relationship charge, so the foundry's margin
  there was at least the sustainable 4 % and its full cost at most about 48.9. Its C_best implies
  49.55 (30 days, December start) to 50.13 (60 days, April start).
- 2026-10-10 `rules` In 14 of 21 case files contract length or volume is ours to pick or left to
  the supplier's standard terms: D01, D02, P03, P04, P07, P08, P09, P10, P14 to P19.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` No alternative, so walking away scores 0: D01, P05, P06, P10, P14, P17.

## Supplier behaviour

- 2026-10-10 `arena` **The round-1 counter is a cap plus claims, not a reaction to the anchor.**
  D01 (quote 52.90), 30 sandbox runs: anchors 44.0 to 48.5 without claims all got 51.30 (-3.0 %);
  a should-cost claim alone 51.00, the order prices alone 50.30, notice or scorecard alone 51.30,
  all three 50.00; the same three claims at anchor 48.88 got 50.40. An insulting anchor (37.03)
  got less (52.30), a shallow one (50.60) 51.40. Words ("what would you need") left the counter at
  51.30 and moved the final (49.40 against 50.00). Distributors (P08, P18): anchor 0.787 of the
  quote got -8 to -10 % in 13 runs; the same sheets and claims gave 5.43 in one run and 5.57 in
  another (supplier-side noise of about 1 %); the order prices and the scorecard "do not change
  our calculation", the forecast is "taken into account" without a visible effect. → Open near
  0.8 of the quote in leverage cases (deeper buys nothing and costs patience), put the claims
  that count into round 1, and treat single-run differences under 2 % as noise.
- 2026-10-10 `arena` **After round 1 each supplier concedes a capped step per round and stops
  after a fixed number of counters.** D01: caps of about 1.6 %, 0.8 %, 0.6 %, 0.4 %, 0.2 % in
  rounds 2 to 6 (0.8 x our move below the cap), final offer in round 6 at the latest or right
  after a move of ours under 0.1 %. Donautal and Werdenfels: 3 counters (r2 +0.04 to +0.20, r3
  0 to +0.15), final in round 2 after a +1 % move, in round 3 after 30 % of the gap, in round 4

  higher price (P08 `5d30fbf219bdc50a` 5.55 to 5.58, P18 `f038c7d05bfee4d6`). Leitner (P07):

  of 0.50 then holds at 45.50 "for 300 ppm and 0 chargeback" (it priced 300 ppm at +0.50 over

"""Plays cases with the policy. The arena answers one call per session at a time and each thread's
60-second clock runs from the supplier's reply, so one loop sends one message at a time, always to
the thread whose clock has run longest; finished threads get a short question before their clock
runs out while the others still negotiate; then the cheapest acceptable sheet is accepted.
`play_waves` is the kit's Live Final loop with this runner."""

import functools
import json
import logging
import threading
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

from arena_kit.client import ArenaError
from arena_kit.play import ENDED, RemoteTable, fetch_documents, latest, moves_left, quota_used_up

from . import llm
from .policy import Negotiator, Side, deadline_near, keepalive_message

log = logging.getLogger("buyer")
RUNS = Path("logs/runs")
KEEPALIVE_AFTER_S = 35  # a finished thread gets a question this long after the supplier's reply
CLOCK_S = 60  # each thread's clock, from the supplier's reply
MARGIN_S = 5  # reserved on every clock for building and delivering the message
FIRST_SEND_S = 10  # what a send (the supplier's reply) takes until we have measured one
CLOSE_TRIES = 3  # a 409 on the close: read what stands now and decide again


def writer_budget(sid, replied, live, send_s, now):
    """Seconds the model may take on the message to `sid`: its own clock must not run out, and
    every other live thread must still get a message once this send returns."""
    left = [CLOCK_S - MARGIN_S - (now - replied[sid])]
    left += [CLOCK_S - MARGIN_S - send_s - (now - replied[o]) for o in live if o != sid]
    return min(llm.TIMEOUT_S, *left)


def play_case(table, case_id, pkg=None, deadline=None, complete=None):
    opened = time.monotonic()  # the supplier clocks run from their first e-mail, before our setup
    case, threads = table.open(case_id)
    if getattr(table, "done", None):  # resumed a case that had already ended
        return table.done
    for events in threads.values():
        for m in events:
            fetch_documents(table, m)
    neg = Negotiator(case, pkg, complete)
    for sid, events in threads.items():
        try:
            neg.setup(sid, events)
            if any(m.get("from") == "buyer" for m in events):  # resumed: continue the path
                neg.restore(sid, events)
        except Exception:  # one supplier's data must not lose the case
            log.exception("%s %s: setup failed", case_id, sid)
            neg.sides.setdefault(sid, Side(sid)).state = "done"
    failed = dict.fromkeys(threads, 0)
    replied = dict.fromkeys(threads, opened)
    send_s = FIRST_SEND_S  # the slowest send so far
    # round 1 goes out cheapest quote first: if a clock runs out, it is the least promising one's
    order = sorted(threads, key=lambda sid: neg.sides[sid].quote or float("inf"))
    rank = {sid: i for i, sid in enumerate(order)}
    result = None

    def open_threads():
        return [s for s in threads if neg.sides[s].state not in ("done", "ended") and live(s)]

    def live(sid):
        return latest(threads[sid]).get("status") not in ENDED

    while not deadline_near(deadline):
        todo = sorted(open_threads(), key=lambda s: (replied[s], rank[s]))
        waiting = [
            s
            for s in threads
            if neg.sides[s].state == "done"
            and live(s)
            and todo
            and time.monotonic() - replied[s] > KEEPALIVE_AFTER_S
            and moves_left(case, threads[s]) - neg.sides[s].late > 0
        ]
        if not todo:
            break
        if waiting:  # a finished bidder whose clock runs out first: keep it alive
            sid = min(waiting, key=lambda s: replied[s])
            message = keepalive_message(threads[sid])
        else:
            sid = todo[0]
            budget = writer_budget(sid, replied, [s for s in threads if live(s)], send_s, time.monotonic())
            try:
                move = neg.move(sid, threads, budget)
            except Exception:  # a field the policy did not expect: the thread must not fall silent
                log.exception("%s %s: move failed", case_id, sid)
                failed[sid] += 1
                if failed[sid] > 2:
                    neg.sides[sid].state = "done"
                    continue
                move = neg.fallback_move(sid, threads)
            if move is None:
                continue
            message = move["message"]
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        try:
            reply = table.send(sid, message)
            send_s = max(send_s, time.monotonic() - t0)
        except ArenaError as e:
            if e.status != 409:
                raise
            log.info("%s %s: %s", case_id, sid, e.detail)
            neg.rollback(sid)  # it never got this message: our last offer stands for it
            reply = table.missed(sid, e)
            if "result" in reply:
                result = reply["result"]
                break
            threads[sid].append(reply)
            replied[sid] = time.monotonic()
            continue
        neg.commit(sid)
        if "result" in reply:  # the reply ended the case, e.g. the last supplier walked away
            result = reply["result"]
            break
        threads[sid] += [{**message, "from": "buyer"}, reply]
        replied[sid] = time.monotonic()
    if result is None:
        for events in threads.values():  # the latest quote PDFs: standard terms for the close
            for m in events[-2:]:
                try:
                    fetch_documents(table, m)
                except ArenaError as e:
                    log.warning("%s: document not fetched: %s", case_id, e)
        result = close(table, case_id, neg, threads)
    save(table.session_id, case_id, neg, result)
    return result


def close(table, case_id, neg, threads):
    """Accept or walk away. A 409 (the sheet expired, the thread ended) means the arena state moved:
    read what stands now and decide again with the same guards. Anything else raises, and the Live
    Final loop resumes the case."""
    for _ in range(CLOSE_TRIES):
        decision = neg.close(threads)
        sid = decision["supplier_id"]
        try:
            return table.close(sid, decision["message"])
        except ArenaError as e:
            if e.status != 409:
                raise
            log.info("%s %s: close refused: %s", case_id, sid, e.detail)
            reply = table.missed(sid, e)
            if "result" in reply:
                return reply["result"]
            threads[sid].append(reply)
    raise RuntimeError(f"{case_id}: no close after {CLOSE_TRIES} tries")


def save(session_id, case_id, neg, result):
    RUNS.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    keep = ("deal", "supplier_id", "terms", "c_open", "c_deal", "c_best", "score")
    path = RUNS / f"{case_id.split(':')[-1]}_{session_id}.json"
    out = {"case": case_id, "session": session_id, "notes": neg.notes, "result": {k: result.get(k) for k in keep}}
    path.write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=1, default=str))


def play_all(client, case_ids, pkg=None, parallel=8, complete=None):
    """Practice or sandbox: many cases at once. {case_id: result or the exception that stopped it}."""
    used_up = threading.Event()

    def one(case_id):
        if used_up.is_set():
            return case_id, ArenaError(429, "not started: the practice quota is used up")
        try:
            return case_id, play_case(RemoteTable(client), case_id, pkg, complete=complete)
        except ArenaError as e:
            if quota_used_up(e):
                used_up.set()
            log.warning("%s: %s", case_id, e)
            return case_id, e
        except Exception as e:  # one broken case must not stop the others
            log.exception("%s failed", case_id)
            return case_id, e

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=parallel) as pool:
        return dict(pool.map(one, case_ids))


def play_waves(client, pkg=None, waves=5, parallel=10, poll=2.0, complete=None):
    """The Live Final: wait for each wave, play its cases in parallel within the wave's cap. No
    human may restart it, so nothing here raises: a failed poll is polled again, a crashed case is
    resumed once (the arena names the running session on a second open)."""
    started, closed, caps = {}, set(), {}

    def one(case, deadline):
        for attempt in range(2):
            try:
                return play_case(RemoteTable(client, case), case["case_id"], pkg, deadline, complete)
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - one broken case must not stop the others
                log.exception("%s failed (attempt %d)", case["case_id"], attempt + 1)
                err = e
                time.sleep(2)
        return err

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=parallel) as pool:
        while len(closed) < waves or not all(f.done() for f in started.values()):
            try:
                cases = client.cases("final")
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - 403 before the first wave, a network blip: poll again
                if not (isinstance(e, ArenaError) and e.status == 403):
                    log.warning("case list: %s", e)
                cases = []
            for case in cases:
                if not case.get("open"):
                    closed.add(case["wave"])
                    continue
                if case.get("seconds_left") is not None:
                    caps[case["wave"]] = time.time() + case["seconds_left"]
                if case["case_id"] not in started and case.get("seconds_left"):
                    log.warning("wave %s: %s", case["wave"], case["case_id"])
                    started[case["case_id"]] = pool.submit(one, case, functools.partial(caps.get, case["wave"]))
            time.sleep(poll)
    return {case_id: f.result() for case_id, f in started.items()}
"""E-mails from templates: every figure and ID comes from code, the wording stays polite and
factual. Never mentions urgency, a budget, our alternative's absence or our target."""

FIELDS = {
    "payment_days": lambda v: f"payment {v} days net",
    "contract_months": lambda v: f"{v} months" if v else "a single order",
    "volume_per_year": lambda v: f"{v} units a year",
    "lead_time_days": lambda v: f"lead time {v} days",
    "effective_date": lambda v: f"valid from {v}",
    "incoterm": lambda v: f"delivery {v}",
    "tooling_eur": lambda v: f"tooling EUR {v:.0f}" if v else "no tooling charge",
    "ppm_commitment": lambda v: f"{v} ppm",
    "chargeback_eur_per_complaint": lambda v: f"chargeback EUR {v:.0f} per complaint",
    "index_clause": lambda v: (
        f"price follows {v.get('series')} on {round((v.get('material_share') or 0) * 100)}% of the price, "
        f"deadband {v.get('deadband_pct') or 0}%"
        if v
        else "fixed price"
    ),
}


def describe(case, sheet):
    parts = [f"EUR {sheet['unit_price']:.2f} per unit"]
    for field in case["negotiable"]:
        if field != "unit_price" and field in sheet and field in FIELDS:
            parts.append(FIELDS[field](sheet[field]))
    fixed = case.get("fixed_terms") or {}
    volume = sheet.get("volume_per_year") or fixed.get("volume_per_year") or case["buyer"]["need_per_year"]
    months = sheet.get("contract_months") or fixed.get("contract_months")
    span = f" over {months} months" if months else ""
    if "volume_per_year" not in case["negotiable"]:
        parts.append(f"for our full demand of {volume} units a year{span}")
    return ", ".join(parts)


# Sandbox D01, identical sheets, only the words varied: plain 50.00, firm 49.90, warm 49.60,
# asking what it needs 49.40 (docs/learnings.md). Asking invites the trade it wants.
ASK = "What would you need from us to move further on the price? We are open to discussing any term that helps you."


def email(case, sheets, claims, statements=(), first=False, moved=False, warm=True, paragraph=None):
    """The e-mail: our words (the model's paragraph, else the template's), then the code sentences
    that answer its asks (figures without IDs), the data arguments and the proposal exactly as code
    computed them."""
    lines = ["Dear Sir or Madam,", ""]
    if first:
        lines.append("Thank you for your offer and for the time your team has put into it.")
    elif moved:
        lines.append("Thank you for your reply and for the step you have taken; we appreciate it.")
    else:
        lines.append("Thank you for your reply.")
    if paragraph:
        lines.append(paragraph)
    elif warm:
        lines.append(
            "We value our cooperation and we understand the cost pressure on your side; we want an agreement "
            "that keeps our partnership healthy for both of us."
        )
    else:
        lines.append("We want an agreement that works for both sides.")
    if statements:
        lines.append("")
        lines += list(statements)
    if claims:
        lines.append("")
        lines += [c["text"] for c in claims]
    lines.append("")
    if len(sheets) == 1:
        lines.append(f"On this basis we propose: {describe(case, sheets[0])}.")
    else:
        lines.append("On this basis we propose one of these packages:")
        lines += [f"- Option {chr(65 + i)}: {describe(case, s)}" for i, s in enumerate(sheets)]
    if first and not paragraph:
        lines += ["", ASK]
    lines += ["", "Kind regards,", "Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing"]
    return "\n".join(lines)


TRAITS = {
    "cash_need": "it is short of cash; when it gets paid matters a lot to it",
